definitions.explanation: The back part of the human foot below the ankle.
The raised part at the back of a shoe.

examples.japanese: ハイヒールの{踵|かかと}が{折|お}れた。
examples.english: The heel of my high heels broke.

examples.japanese: {走|はし}りすぎて{踵|かかと}にまめができた。
examples.english: I got a blister on my heel from running too much.

examples.japanese: {踵|かかと}を{上|あ}げてつま{先|さき}で{立|た}った。
examples.english: I raised my heels and stood on my toes.

examples.japanese: {乾燥|かんそう}して{踵|かかと}がひび{割|わ}れている。
examples.english: My heels are cracked from dryness.

examples.japanese: {靴|くつ}の{踵|かかと}がすり{減|へ}っている。
examples.english: The heels of my shoes are worn down.

examples.japanese: {踵|かかと}の{高|たか}い{靴|くつ}は{歩|ある}きにくい。
examples.english: Shoes with high heels are hard to walk in.

examples.japanese: {踵|かかと}を{修理|しゅうり}に{出|だ}した。
{新|あたら}しい{靴|くつ}の{踵|かかと}が{硬|かた}くて{足|あし}が{痛|いた}くなった。
examples.english: The heels of my new shoes were so stiff that my feet started hurting.

examples.japanese: {踵|かかと}から{着地|ちゃくち}するのが{正|ただ}しい{歩|ある}き{方|かた}だと{言|い}われている。
examples.english: It's said that landing on the heel is the correct way to walk.

notes:
{踵|かかと} refers to both the body part and the shoe part.

OFTEN IN HIRAGANA:
This word is very frequently written as かかと due to the kanji's complexity.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {踵|かかと}が{高|たか}い (high heels)
- {踵|かかと}を{返|かえ}す (turn on one's heel)
- {踵|かかと}を{上|あ}げる (raise one's heels, stand on tiptoe)

BODY PART CONTEXT:
Other foot parts:
- {足首|あしくび} (ankle)
- {足|あし}の{裏|うら} (sole of foot)
- つま{先|さき} (toe/tiptoe)
- {足|あし}の{指|ゆび} (toes)

IDIOM:
{踵|かかと}を{接|せっ}して = in close succession, one after another (literally: heels touching)
